findings.highlight: I sit down on my futon
findings.evidenceJa: どさん、と布団に腰を落とす
findings.governingReading: Shirou drops heavily onto the futon with a thud after the fruitless patrol.
findings.explanation: The English removes the weight and discouragement carried by his movement.

findings.highlight: Even a human could match Zouken or Assassin
findings.evidenceJa: 打倒できる相手
findings.governingReading: Zouken and Assassin remain opponents that human beings can potentially defeat.
findings.explanation: The English changes defeatability into the weaker and tactically different ability to match them.

findings.evidenceJa: だがあの二人は違う
findings.governingReading: The contrast shifts from Zouken and Assassin to the other two threats: Saber and the black shadow.
findings.explanation: The English demonstrative most naturally points back to Zouken and Assassin, obscuring the intended division of the four enemies.

findings.highlight: as long as there are victims
findings.evidenceJa: 街に犠牲者が出た以上
findings.governingReading: Because civilian victims have already appeared in the city, Shirou can no longer accept inability to win as an answer.
findings.explanation: The English changes a completed threshold event into an ongoing conditional state.

findings.highlight: we can’t just ignore them saying we can’t beat them
findings.evidenceJa: 済まされる状況じゃない
findings.governingReading: The civilian toll means they cannot let matters end with the excuse that the enemies are unbeatable.
findings.explanation: The English introduces an unclear plural object and malformed speech relation.

findings.evidenceJa: 止まっていた血が流れ始める
findings.governingReading: As the tightly bound cloth loosens, blood that had been stopped begins circulating again.
findings.explanation: The English invents flow into the arm instead of restored circulation.

findings.highlight: sitting on a mountain of swords
findings.evidenceJa: 剣山に座っている
findings.governingReading: The futon feels like sitting on a kenzan, a dense bed or pincushion of spikes.
findings.explanation: The English literalizes the characters as a mountain of swords and changes the tactile image.

findings.highlight: Time slows to an impossible crawl
findings.evidenceJa: 時間が猛スピードで減速していく
findings.governingReading: Time decelerates at tremendous speed in Shirou’s distorted perception.
findings.explanation: The English removes the deliberate speed/deceleration collision and adds an unsupported judgment of impossibility.

findings.evidenceJa: 狂想的なイメージ
findings.governingReading: The flashback stalls in rhapsodic, frenzied imagery.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes the broad and potentially positive “fantastic” and leaves the phrase grammatically damaged.

findings.evidenceJa: 跪いた自分の頭が、どん、と畳に倒れる
findings.governingReading: After dropping to his knees, Shirou’s head falls with a thud onto the tatami.
findings.explanation: The English removes his kneeling collapse, the thud, and the tatami surface.

findings.highlight: A natural fear for any living thing
findings.evidenceJa: 生物として当たり前の畏怖
findings.governingReading: Shirou experiences the fear of extinction natural to a living organism.
findings.explanation: The English preposition makes the phrase read as fear directed toward a living thing rather than an organism’s innate fear.

findings.highlight: It’s not because I want to live
findings.evidenceJa: 生きたいから死にたくないのではない
findings.governingReading: His rejection of death does not arise from wanting to live and therefore not wanting to die.
findings.explanation: The English omits the resulting desire not to die and leaves only half of the logical relation.

findings.evidenceJa: 何度も何度も引き絞った
findings.governingReading: Shirou pulls the knot tight over and over so it can never loosen again.
findings.explanation: The English removes the desperate repetition.

findings.evidenceJa: 嗚咽を漏らしながら泣いた
findings.governingReading: Shirou cries while involuntary sobs escape him.
findings.explanation: The English changes sobbing into a groan.

findings.highlight: when I loosened the cloth and my shoulder touched the outside air
findings.evidenceJa: わずかに緩め、肩が外気に触れただけ
findings.governingReading: Merely loosening the cloth slightly and exposing only the shoulder to outside air is enough to damage his awareness.
findings.explanation: The English removes both minimizers, making the exposure sound broader.

findings.evidenceJa: 意識がボロボロと欠けた
findings.governingReading: Pieces of Shirou’s consciousness break off raggedly under the exposure.
findings.explanation: The English suggests consciousness disappears wholesale rather than losing fragments.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=カラダ char=2]廃線
findings.governingReading: The written image is an abandoned railway read as “body,” which then runs toward its terminal station.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only body and erases the railway metaphor that motivates the terminal station.

findings.evidenceJa: 息が荒い
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s breathing is ragged or harsh.
findings.explanation: The English uses an unnatural idiom and personifies the breath as running wild.

findings.evidenceJa: よくわからないあたまで堪える
findings.governingReading: Still crouched, Shirou endures incomprehensible pain with an equally incomprehensible or disordered mind.
findings.explanation: The English omits the impaired mental state through which he experiences the pain.

findings.highlight: I can’t remember how to recollect anything in the past
findings.evidenceJa: 一秒前に思いを馳せる、という方法が思い出せなかった
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot remember even the method of directing thought back a single second.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the precise immediate-memory failure into inability to recollect anything in the past.

findings.evidenceJa: 痛みが引いていく
findings.governingReading: The pain is in the process of receding.
findings.explanation: The English presents the pain as fully gone.

findings.evidenceJa: 断絶した意識をなんとかヒトまとめにする
findings.governingReading: Shirou somehow manages to gather his severed consciousness into one human-shaped whole.
findings.explanation: The English removes fragmentation, difficulty, and the marked ヒト wording.

findings.evidenceJa: タンタンと包丁を入れた玉葱
findings.governingReading: His scattered memories resemble onions rhythmically struck by a kitchen knife.
findings.explanation: The English retains chopped onions but removes the knife and rhythmic sensory detail.

findings.highlight: See, I can add color with soy sauce, add flavor with pepper, and add some potato starch to complete the dish.
findings.evidenceJa: じゅー、じゅっじゅっ
findings.governingReading: The damaged cooking hallucination includes the repeated sound of sizzling.
findings.explanation: The English removes the sound entirely.

findings.evidenceJa: 歪だがマトマリのある傷めモノ
findings.governingReading: The seasonings produce a misshapen but cohering “damaged thing,” punning against stir-fried food.
findings.explanation: The English sanitizes the injured, distorted mental product into completion of an ordinary dish.

findings.highlight: My head is good for nothing
findings.evidenceJa: お節介なまでに人の手が入りまくった頭
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s head has been interfered with and worked over by other hands to an almost meddlesome degree.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the invasive history with a generic judgment that his head is useless.

findings.highlight: Nobody relies on something that’s not there
findings.evidenceJa: 無いものを頼りとする事自体が、既に正順ではない
findings.governingReading: Shirou concludes that relying on what he has already lost is itself outside the proper order.
findings.explanation: The English universalizes the thought into a banal rule and removes the moral or structural disorder.

findings.highlight: something I must suppress using all my life
findings.evidenceJa: 一生涯をかけて封殺する物
findings.governingReading: He regards the foreign arm as something to seal away over the whole course of his life.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and obscures the lifetime commitment.

findings.highlight: I still hold on to my left arm
findings.evidenceJa: 未練がましく左腕を抱いた
findings.governingReading: Despite understanding the implied escape, Shirou clutches the arm with lingering attachment and reluctance to relinquish it.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the hold but removes his emotional attachment.

findings.evidenceJa: こめかみに
findings.governingReading: The imagined gun muzzle is pressed to Shirou’s temple.
findings.explanation: The English moves it to his forehead.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=トリガー char=2]撃鉄
findings.governingReading: The arm is written as the gun’s hammer and read as “trigger,” fusing two activation images.
findings.explanation: The English retains only trigger and erases the written hammer layer.

findings.evidenceJa: 定められた機能にそって
findings.governingReading: Once activated, the arm follows its predetermined function like a gun firing a bullet through his head.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the trigger sequence but omits its mechanical inevitability as a fixed function.

findings.evidenceJa: 薄闇に息を潜め
findings.governingReading: Shirou makes himself still and quiet in the dim darkness.
findings.explanation: The English removes the surrounding dimness and literalizes the hushed posture as holding his breath.

findings.evidenceJa: 空白の壁
findings.governingReading: Shirou stares at a blank, vacant wall in the dim room.
findings.explanation: The English invents the wall’s color.

findings.evidenceJa: もう一度左腕を強く抱いて
findings.governingReading: Shirou once again clutches his left arm tightly before lying down.
findings.explanation: The English omits repetition, side, and force.

findings.evidenceJa: つまらない弱音を飲み込んで
findings.governingReading: Shirou swallows an unworthy expression of weakness and chooses sleep for the next day.
findings.explanation: The English turns suppressed, unvoiced weakness into audible whimpering that has run its course.
